cft_lead: A template says how to check a stack. JGates applies the ones from the catalog and from your project according to what it finds in the components.
cft_none_project: No project template yet. Create one for a stack the catalog does not cover.
cft_details_aria: See the details of the template {name}
cft_required_reason: Required: it is always applied, and turning it off would leave the plan without this base.
cft_governed_reason: Governed mode: the templates are fixed by the policy {policy} and do not change here.
cft_created: Template {id} created in {folder} and registered in jgates.yml.
cft_order_lead: From weakest to strongest: what comes later replaces what comes before.
cft_create_lead: Creates a file in {folder} from the model: it extends base, matches a stack and declares one check by generic command.
cft_create_id_help: Lowercase letters, numbers, dot, hyphen and underscore. Example: go-service.
cft_create_command_help: Example: go test ./... . The command becomes a vector, never a shell line.
cft_create_evidence_help: The exit code alone proves little: it never covers security, architecture or tests by itself.
cft_d_chain_lead: From the ancestor to the template: each one shows what it defines. The badge marks the field that replaces an ancestor's.
cft_unreferenced_help: The file {source} exists, but jgates.yml does not use it.
cft_adopt_aria: Use the template {name} in this project
cft_delete_lead: The template {id} leaves jgates.yml and its file in .jgates/templates is deleted. The checks it brought stop running.
cft_w_edit_lead: Changes only what the model guides: the name, the stack, the command, the effects and the evidence. The rest of the file stays as it is.
cft_w_not_editable: This file does not have the shape of the model (one generic-command check). Edit it in the YAML tab.
cft_w_id_invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore, starting with a letter or digit.
cft_w_capability_help: The capability says what kind of proof the command gives (tests, lint, security...).
cft_w_match_help: Choose the languages and frameworks it matches. The project components with that stack start using it.
cft_w_match_none: Without a language or framework, the template only applies when someone asks for it.
cft_w_match_some: It applies to the components that have the chosen languages and frameworks.
cft_w_executable_help: Only the program, without arguments. Example: go.
cft_w_args_help: One field per argument. Spaces and quotes inside a field stay in the same argument: nothing is split or passed through a shell.
cft_w_review_help: These are the files that change. Nothing is written before you confirm.
